short: Convolutional denoising AE features (M06) are standard: speckle denoising predates it; 6.17% vs DCT 6.58% at equal length is ~4 of 1023 words, single runs, one speaker.
position: The paper [@li2019denoising] changes one component, the ultrasound feature extractor (M06), replacing DCT or a fully connected autoencoder with a convolutional autoencoder trained on speckle-corrupted inputs; it is standard. Speckle denoising of tongue ultrasound predates it [@jaumardhakoun2016articulatory], so the "first attempt" (§4) holds only for the convolutional variant. The headline 6.17% against the "state-of-the-art" 6.45% (Abstract) sets length 60 against DCT at length 30; at equal length the margin is 0.41 points, about 4 words of the 1023-word test [@ji2018updating] (inference), from unrepeated runs on one speaker. Denoising adds 0.05 points over the plain convolutional autoencoder (Table 2), so the evidence supports convolution, not denoising. The eight new WERs in Table 2 are not whole error counts over 1023 words, while the two that equal Ji et al.'s published values are (inference), and the paper does not say how they were obtained.
